chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayabah, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, in the Book of Ali عليه السلام: If a man were to cut his wife’s private part, I would obligate him to pay her her full diyyah. If he does not pay the diyyah to her, I would cut his private part for her if she demands that.

key_terms.إِنْ طَلَبَتْ ذَلِكَ: If she demands that legal remedy
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: The prescribed financial compensation for injury
key_terms.دِيَتَهَا: Her blood money compensation for bodily injury
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: The written legal record attributed to Imam Ali عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man cuts his wife’s private part in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a legal ruling from the Book of Imam Ali عليه السلام concerning severe bodily injury inflicted by a husband upon his wife. It establishes her right to full blood money (diyyah), and if that is not paid, it affirms retaliatory punishment upon her demand.
